title: Discovery - Redwood Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private (Latency/Throughput)
transcript:
[00:00] Avery: Hey everyone, thanks for joining. Quick intro — Avery from Redwood AE, Marco SE. We got about 45 minutes. Priya: thanks, we have Janelle and Daniel on as well, want to get into latency targets and whether we should go hosted/dedicated/private.
[00:20] Marco: Great. Can you share current production workload? token sizes, concurrency?
[00:30] Priya: Sure, today we run a mix of short prompts — 20-50 tokens — and some long-form summarization ~1,200 tokens. P95 latency goal for chat is around 400ms right now, ideally down to 200-300ms for short flows. Concurrency: we see spikes to 150 concurrent sessions, sustained 50-60.
[00:55] Daniel: Also want streaming for typing UX. Token/sec throughput is a concern because we pay a lot for hosted API calls.
[01:10] Marco: Understand. For Redwood hosted, typical p95 for short prompts on our curated models is often sub-250ms in our benchmarks at moderate concurrency, but depends on model size and prompt prep. For heavy concurrency 100+, dedicated pools are recommended.
[01:35] Priya: When you say "dedicated" — do you mean reserved GPU pools with pinned nodes? How does fallback work if we exceed reserved capacity?
[01:45] Avery: Yes, Dedicated = reserved GPU pools. We support autoscale policies and burst to a shared capacity tier. We can also configure graceful fallback to a smaller/lighter model or to hosted capacity.
[02:05] Janelle: Security wise we need VPC and KMS integrations. We are regulated — need SOC2 and audit logs.
[02:15] Marco: We support Private deployment (VPC or on-prem) for air-gapped needs, with KMS/HSM integration and audit log exports. SOC 2 is available for hosted and dedicated; Private has additional compliance options.
[02:35] Priya: Back to performance: our main question — p95 and tokens/sec. Can you run a token/sec bench with our typical mix?
[02:45] Marco: Absolutely, we usually run a tokens/sec benchmark across model variants and quantization profiles. For Llama-2-13B-ish models with int8 quant, we see 800-1,200 tokens/sec per GPU for streaming generation on A100-like hardware; with batching and kv-prefix caching you can get effective system throughput higher. For larger models or CPU/low-tier GPU it's lower.
[03:15] Daniel: What's the impact of streaming on p95? We need low first-token latency for UX.
[03:25] Marco: Streaming is mostly about first-byte latency. We tune kernel selection and size of generate chunking. A common pattern: smaller chunk sizes reduce first-token latency but increase overhead. We aim for 100-200ms first-token p95 for small prompts on optimized stacks.
[03:50] Priya: Do you support chunked streaming while maintaining KV cache across streams? We have multi-turn chat and don't want to re-encode prefix each request.
[04:00] Marco: Yes, KV cache persisted per session on the runtime. For dedicated/private you get more control over session locality which helps p95 consistency under concurrency.
[04:20] Janelle: Cost tradeoffs — how much more expensive is dedicated vs hosted?
[04:30] Avery: Dedicated is reserved monthly/annual commitment; unit cost lower per token for sustained throughput but you bear reserved capacity. Hosted is pay-as-you-go with slightly higher per-token cost but no commit. We can share a pricing model tailored to your concurrency profile.
[04:55] Priya: For a pilot, can we test both hosted and dedicated modes?
[05:05] Avery: Yes, we typically do a hybrid POC: start on hosted for quick benchmarks and then spin up a small dedicated pool for sustained load testing.
[05:15] Daniel: Any additional tuning suggestions? We saw big improvements with prefix caching and dynamic batching on our side.
[05:25] Marco: Exactly — recommend sample-based batching strategies: prioritize latency SLOs and have a burst buffer for throughput. Also model compilation and kernel selection matters; we can run model profiles and recommend quantization (int8/4) if acceptable for quality.
[05:50] Priya: Quality/regression monitoring? If we quant or move models, we need eval hooks.
[05:58] Marco: Redwood Optimize ties to evals and regression alerts with prompt sets. We can run A/B comparisons and rollback policies during rollouts.
[06:15] Janelle: For privacy we need data retention controls and query logging off for Private.
[06:24] Avery: We support retention policies and ability to disable logging in Private; for hosted/dedicated we have configurable retention windows and exportable audit logs.
[06:40] Priya: Quick numbers request — can you give an example p95 vs concurrency curve?
[06:48] Marco: Sure. Example rough curve on our 13B quantized model on an A100 class node: at concurrency 1 p95 ~120ms, concurrency 20 p95 ~160ms with batching, concurrency 100 p95 ~280-400ms depending on burstiness. For a 70B model these numbers shift up (p95 1-> 250ms, 20-> 450ms, 100-> 800ms).
[07:20] Daniel: How deterministic are these numbers? We need SLOs for SLAs.
[07:28] Marco: We provide typical percentiles based on observed workloads; Dedicated with reserved nodes gives much tighter variance and we offer SLA-backed uptime and latency tiers. Hosted is subject to multi-tenant variance but we provide percentile baselines.
[07:45] Priya: For streaming UX, we need <300ms p95 end-to-end for short chat. Doable with hosted?
[07:55] Marco: For many customers, yes on hosted if you pick smaller model or our optimized variants. But if you need strict SLO at scale (150 concurrent sessions) dedicated is recommended.
[08:15] Janelle: Architecture question: how does routing handle region and failover?
[08:24] Avery: Smart routing can route by latency/cost/region and fallback to compatible model variant or region. We can also pin traffic for residency.
[08:38] Priya: Let's talk about tokenization — we see variance in token counts across models. Does Redwood normalize billing or provide token mapping?
[08:48] Avery: Billing is per-token according to chosen model unit. We provide tokenization utilities and per-token cost breakdown in the Console so you can map expected cost across model variants.
[09:05] Daniel: For the benchmark, what artifacts do you need from us? workload samples? concurrency profile?
[09:12] Marco: Send a sample prompt corpus with token distribution, desired p95 targets, and a test account or API key. We'll run both hosted and dedicated benchmarks with representative concurrency and streaming enabled.
[09:30] Priya: How long do benchmarks take?
[09:33] Marco: Roughly 1-2 days of runs to get stable p95 at target concurrency and various burst patterns. We'll iterate on config (batch sizes, chunk sizes).
[09:45] Janelle: Regarding private deploy — what's the deployment footprint? GPUs required?
[09:52] Marco: Private can run on customer-provided infra, typically GPU nodes (A100/H100 or similar) or on our appliance. We publish recommended configs (GPU type, memory, NVMe for cache). For smaller scale we can deploy CPU-only but latency increases significantly.
[10:12] Priya: Any gotchas about KV cache eviction or multi-tenant cache contamination?
[10:18] Marco: We isolate per-customer sessions; cache eviction policies configurable. In multi-tenant hosted, we use per-request namespace keys to avoid contamination. In Dedicated/Private you have stronger locality guarantees.
[10:35] Daniel: Ok, one more — can you stream partial tokens with SSE or websockets?
[10:40] Marco: We support streaming via chunked HTTP and websockets, SSE emulation. The SDKs provide streaming hooks.
[10:52] Priya: Are there examples of customers that moved from hosted to dedicated due to latency?
[10:58] Avery: Yes — several scale-ups who started on hosted and then committed to Dedicated once concurrency and SLOs tightened. We can anonymize case studies and share numbers.
[11:10] Janelle: On the security checklist, can you share SOC2 report and KMS integration docs?
[11:16] Avery: We'll share SOC2 and security pack.
[11:20] Priya: Let's recap next steps and action items.
[11:25] Avery: Recap: Redwood will run tokens/sec and p95 benchmarks on hosted and a small dedicated pool using your sample corpus; provide security docs; share pricing and recommended config.
[11:35] Daniel: Also want a plan for a 2-week pilot with streaming enabled and metrics collection.
[11:40] Marco: We'll instrument traces and token-level breakdowns in the Console and provide per-route dashboards for the pilot.
[11:48] Janelle: And list of required infra for Private deploy.
[11:52] Avery: Yep. We'll follow up with docs and timeline. Thanks all.
[11:58] (call ends)
summary: Discovery call focused on p95 latency targets, concurrency, streaming UX, and tokens/sec benchmarking. Customer (Acme AI) seeks guidance on Hosted vs Dedicated vs Private. Redwood team proposed hybrid POC: initial hosted benchmarks then small dedicated pool for sustained load; offered to run tokens/sec and p95 benchmarks, share SOC2/security docs, and provide pricing and infra guidance.
